glossario.simples: The text of a law that is still being discussed and voted on. In Portuguese: {{projeto de lei}} (PL).
When citizens themselves present a bill, with many signatures.
The lawmaker in charge of studying a bill and giving a report on it. In Portuguese: {{relator}}.
The written opinion of the rapporteur or of the committee: approve, change or reject the bill. In Portuguese: {{parecer}}.
The House that checks and reviews a bill that the other House has already approved. In Portuguese: {{Casa revisora}}.
When the president agrees with the bill and signs it. Then it becomes law.
When the president disagrees and blocks the whole bill or a part of it.
The official newspaper of the federal government, where laws are published. In Portuguese: {{Diário Oficial da União}}.
The minimum number of lawmakers or votes required in a vote.
More than half of all the members of the House, counting even those who are absent.
More than half of the lawmakers present at the vote.
A type of law for subjects where the Constitution asks for more votes.
{{Proposta de Emenda à Constituição}} (proposed constitutional amendment): a bill to change the Constitution.
A rule that the president creates in urgent cases. It applies right away, but only for a while. In Portuguese: {{medida provisória}} (MP).
A decision of Congress on matters that only Congress decides, without going to the president.
An act of the president that details how a law must be carried out.
The rounds of voting on a proposal. In Portuguese: {{turnos}}.
To officially declare that a new law or amendment exists.
The parts of the Constitution that not even an amendment can abolish. In Portuguese: {{cláusulas pétreas}} (“stone clauses”).
The division of power into Executive, Legislative and Judiciary, so that no one is in charge alone.
Brazil organized into the Union, the states, the Federal District and the municipalities, each with its own autonomy.
Freedom to make your own decisions, within the rules.
The plan for how much money the government will receive and how it will spend it during the year.
{{Lei de Diretrizes Orçamentárias}} (Budget Guidelines Law): the rules and priorities for preparing the next year's budget.
{{Lei Orçamentária Anual}} (Annual Budget Law): the budget for the year, with what the government expects to collect and can spend.
Choices made by deputies and senators about where to spend part of the budget money. In Portuguese: {{emendas parlamentares}}.
To gather money, mainly through taxes.
The federal deputies and the senators from the same state, together. In Portuguese: {{bancada estadual}}.
Congress's vacation: at the end of July and from the end of December to the beginning of February.
Days of work: Monday to Friday, not counting holidays.
The head of the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office ({{Ministério Público da União}}), which defends society and demands that laws be followed.
The highest courts in the country after the STF, like the STJ and the TSE.
{{Supremo Tribunal Federal}} (Supreme Federal Court): the highest court in the country, which takes care of the Constitution.
The most important law of the country. All other laws must respect it.

slides.titulo: Every law starts with an idea
slides.texto: Then the idea follows a path with several steps until it becomes a law that applies to everyone.
Move square by square. Example: an ordinary bill that starts in the Chamber of Deputies.

passos.txt: Someone sees a problem and thinks of a solution. Made-up example: a drinking fountain in every playground.

The idea becomes a text: the **bill** (projeto de lei). Deputies, senators, committees and the President of the Republic can present one. On some subjects, so can the STF, the superior courts and the Prosecutor General of the Republic. And citizens too!
Groups of deputies study the bill. A rapporteur (relator) gives a report, and the committee votes.
All the deputies vote. Many bills skip this square: they are decided only in the committees.
The bill goes to the Senate, the reviewing House. If the Senate changes the text, the bill goes back to the Chamber to decide.
The President of the Republic has 15 working days. The president can approve (**sanction**) or block (veto) all of it or a part.
If there is a veto, deputies and senators decide together whether it stays or falls.
The law comes out in the Official Gazette ({{Diário Oficial da União}}). If it does not set a date, it takes effect 45 days later.

slides.titulo: Not every proposal is the same
slides.texto: Each type has its own purpose and needs a different number of votes.

cards.txt: The ordinary law, for most subjects.
cards.mais: To vote, the session needs at least 257 deputies (or 41 senators) present. Then the bill passes if it gets the majority of the votes.

cards.txt: For subjects where the Constitution asks for a complementary law.
Changes the text of the Constitution.
cards.mais: Who can propose one: 1/3 of the deputies (171) or of the senators (27). Also the President of the Republic, or more than half of the state Legislative Assemblies. Once it is approved, Congress itself promulgates the amendment.

cards.txt: The president creates it only in cases of “relevance and urgency”: an important subject that is in a hurry. It applies right away.

dados.val: The Chamber and the Senate must approve it

cards.mais: If it is not approved in time, it expires. Some subjects cannot be handled by an MP, like election rules and crimes.

cards.txt: For subjects that only Congress decides, like approving agreements with other countries.
cards.mais: It is also with a legislative decree that Congress sets the salaries of deputies, senators, the president and ministers.

cards.txt: The president uses it to detail how a law will be carried out. A decree does not create a new law.
cards.mais: If a decree goes beyond the limits of the law, Congress can suspend that decree.

slides.titulo: Three ways to count a majority
slides.texto: In a vote, having more votes is not always enough. Imagine a class of **30 students** voting on a new rule:

itens: You need more than half of those who are present.
Those who are absent do not count.
colunas.exemplo: 20 students came: 11 vote “yes” and 9 vote “no”. Approved!

itens: You need more than half of the **whole** class.
Those who are absent count as if they had not voted “yes”.
colunas.exemplo: Class of 30: you need **16** “yes” votes, even if many people are absent.

itens: You need 3 out of every 5 students in the whole class.
It is the hardest to reach.

slides.titulo: How many “yes” votes are needed in Congress?
slides.texto: Choose what is being voted on and watch the seats light up.

opcoes.explica: It needs a **simple majority**: more than half of those who voted. But the vote only counts if at least half of the House is there: 257 deputies or 41 senators. That minimum is the **quorum**.

casas.rot: Example: if 300 deputies vote, 151 “yes” votes approve it.
Example: if 50 senators vote, 26 “yes” votes approve it.

opcoes.explica: It needs an **absolute majority**: more than half of all the members, counting even those who are absent.

casas.rot: “yes” votes at least, out of 513 deputies.
“yes” votes at least, out of 81 senators.

opcoes.explica: Deputies and senators vote in the same session of Congress. To override the President's **veto**, an **absolute majority** is needed in both Houses.

casas.rot: deputies voting to override the veto.
senators voting to override the veto.

opcoes.explica: This is the hardest: it needs **3/5** of each House. And a **PEC** is voted on twice in the Chamber and twice in the Senate (two **rounds**).

casas.rot: “yes” votes at least, out of 513 deputies, in each round.
“yes” votes at least, out of 81 senators, in each round.

slides.texto: Once approved by Congress, the bill goes to the President of the Republic.

itens.txt: **Sanction**: the president agrees and signs. The bill becomes law.
**Veto**: the president blocks the whole bill (total veto) or just a part of it (partial veto).
The deadline is 15 working days. If the president stays silent, it counts as a sanction.
A veto needs a reason: the bill goes against the Constitution or against the public interest.
Then deputies and senators review the veto together. To override it: 257 deputies and 41 senators.

slides.titulo: A law that started with signatures

quadros.txt: For more than a year, citizens' movements collected more than 1.5 million signatures across the country.
In September 2009, the bill arrived at the Chamber. Since the Chamber had no way to check so many signatures, a group of deputies signed the bill.
In May 2010, the Chamber and then the Senate approved the bill.
On June 4, 2010, the president signed it. Complementary Law 135 was born: the **Clean Record Law** ({{Lei da Ficha Limpa}}).
The law increased the number of situations that stop someone from running for office. One example: being convicted of certain crimes by a group of judges.

slides.moral: Citizens can also propose laws: this is **popular initiative**. The rule requires signatures from at least 1% of the country's voters, from at least 5 states.

slides.titulo: What not even a PEC can take away
slides.texto: Some parts of the Constitution cannot be abolished. They are the **entrenched clauses** ({{cláusulas pétreas}}; {{pétrea}} means “made of stone”).

itens.txt: Direct, secret, universal and periodic voting: everyone votes for the candidates, in secret, from time to time.
The separation of powers: Executive, Legislative and Judiciary.
Each person's rights and guarantees, like freedom.
The federation: Brazil divided into the Union, the states, the DF and the municipalities, each with its own autonomy.

slides.coruja: A PEC that tries to abolish these parts cannot even be voted on!

slides.titulo: The budget is a law too
slides.texto: Every year, the government plans how much money it will collect and how it will spend it. Congress reviews the plan, changes it and approves it.

itens.txt: **LDO** (Budget Guidelines Law): the rules and priorities for the next year's budget. The president sends it by April 15.
**LOA** (Annual Budget Law): the budget for the year, with the money for health, schools, roads... It reaches Congress by August 31.
With parliamentary amendments, deputies and senators choose where to spend a part: a public works project, a health clinic...
As a rule, the government must pay the individual amendments and those of the state caucus. Half of the individual ones go to health.
In 2024, a new law created rules for these amendments.

slides.coruja: Until the LDO is approved, Congress cannot leave for its July recess!

slides.pergunta: To change the Constitution, how many votes does a PEC need in the Chamber?
slides.explica: A PEC needs 3/5 of the deputies: 308 votes, in two rounds. In the Senate, it needs 49.

slides.pergunta: The president received a bill and did not answer within 15 working days. What happens?
opcoes: The bill goes back to the Chamber
slides.explica: The president's silence counts as a sanction, and the bill becomes law.
